newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest grains futures limit down on Chicago fall.
newsitem.headline: Budapest grains futures limit down on Chicago fall.

text.p: Most grains futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) went limit down on Tuesday due to Chicago's falls on Monday and on expectations of a good wheat crop, traders said.
Milling wheat dropped the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all positions to end at between 20,820 forints for July and 24,810 for May 1998.
"Chicago wheat prices dropped (on Monday) by the equivalent of an average 800 forints," said Janos Szolyka of Swap brokerage.
He added the wheat crop forecast released on Monday by the Agriculture Ministry also pushed prices down amid strong selling pressure on the market.
Maize futures finished 210 to 400 forints lower for all maturities except October which held unchanged at 19,610 forints.
Feed barley and sunflower seed futures were mostly limit-down while feed wheat futures were untraded.
Total grains futures turnover rose to 1,212 lots or 534.34 million forints from Monday's 692 lots or 305.57 million forints.
Milling wheat futures accounted for half the total turnover with 653 lots changing hands.
